'''Sophie Brasselet''' is a French [[Optics|optical physicist]] whose research interests include [[nonlinear optics]], the optical and [[fluorescence|fluorescent]] properties of [[biomolecule]]s, the [[Optical tweezers|optical manipulation of molecules]], and the development of instrumentation for biological imaging, over scales ranging from single molecules to multi-cellular tissues. She is a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), and the director of the [[Fresnel Institute]] in [[Marseille]] ([[France]]) also affiliated with the Mosaic advanced photonics group within the institute.{{r|brillouin}}

==Education and career==
Brasselet studied optics and photonics as a student at the [[Institut d'optique Graduate School|École supérieure d'optique]], completing her studies in 1994. She went on to a doctorate in 1997 at [[Paris-Sud University]], under the supervision of [[Joseph Zyss]].{{r|fresnel}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Stanford University]] in California with [[William E. Moerner]], she returned to France in 2000 as an assistant professor at the [[École normale supérieure Paris-Saclay|École normale supérieure de Cachan]]. In 2006, she moved to [[Aix-Marseille University]] and in 2009 she was named a director of research within the CNRS.{{r|fresnel}}

==Recognition==
Brasselet received the [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2016.{{r|argent}} In 2022 she won the Léon Brillouin grand prize of the French Optical Society (La Société Française d'Optique), the first female winner of this prize.{{r|brillouin}}

She was named a Fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica]], in the 2022 class of fellows, "for advancing fundamental knowledge of molecular nonlinear optics and application to polarization-resolved nonlinear and super resolution orientation microscopy".{{r|optica}}
